### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx`  _(via get_metadata_item (literal, a string literal in DEFINITION_READER_TOOL_NAMES))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cceb5c626d3c68a457e1dcf20de1fea0e0194366` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a24c845d07c900931e28eb7a30ed1a94514cbf2a` — the merge of head `beadd87426a43360203ba7910228d2c121ba55ef` into base `cceb5c626d3c68a457e1dcf20de1fea0e0194366`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a24c845d07c900931e28eb7a30ed1a94514cbf2a && git checkout a24c845d07c900931e28eb7a30ed1a94514cbf2a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cceb5c626d3c68a457e1dcf20de1fea0e0194366 beadd87426a43360203ba7910228d2c121ba55ef && git checkout -B drift-repro cceb5c626d3c68a457e1dcf20de1fea0e0194366 && git merge --no-ff beadd87426a43360203ba7910228d2c121ba55ef

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cceb5c626d3c68a457e1dcf20de1fea0e0194366
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cceb5c626d3c68a457e1dcf20de1fea0e0194366` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review — PASS at 01e6d0f64499d4c0e02ea45480eaf62a07092cae

Head-sha: `01e6d0f64499d4c0e02ea45480eaf62a07092cae`
Local-runs: probe — main's `readClause2Line` (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`) over this head's changeset text, to read the declaration's value and arm; nothing built or tested locally

Face: the `Clause-②: yes` declaration alone. `record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths` over the four changed paths reads the declaration face, `TIER_DEFAULT`. The diff has no `packages/spec/src/**` path, no governed path and no `(narrowing)` arm, so it does not escalate to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Read at 2026-11-20T06:09Z. The head has not moved since dispatch, and it merges cleanly onto origin/main `cceb5c62`.

### ① Derived judgments

Card #35633 "Done when", item by item:

1. **`packageDocAnswerRule(definitionReader?)` from the barrel**: met. `export function packageDocAnswerRule(definitionReader?: string): string` in `mcp-server-runtime.ts` is re-exported in `src/index.ts`. The package `exports` map has only `.` (`dist/index`, built from `src/index.ts`), so this is the published surface.
2. **`packageDocToolsServed(...)` with the reader-name list the rule needs**: met. It is re-exported from `mcp-http-tools.ts`, and that file is not in the diff. `DEFINITION_READER_TOOL_NAMES` and a pure `definitionReaderOf(toolNames)` are exported beside it. The card's alternative, `definitionReaderServed`, takes the open server's `McpAuthoringInjection`, so the name-list form is the better contract for a host.
3. **One copy of the text**: met. `openServerInstructions` still calls `packageDocAnswerRule(docRule.definitionReader)`, and `definitionReaderServed` now delegates to `definitionReaderOf`. The diff adds no second copy of the sentence.
4. **A test pins the barrel export**: met. `package-doc-answer-rule-barrel-35633.test.ts` imports all four from `./index.js`, the source of the sole `exports['.']` entry. A self-import of `@objectstack/mcp` would need a built `dist`, so the source barrel is the right pin. For each case (no reader, `get_metadata_item`, `describe_metadata`), it asserts that the default `initialize` text holds `packageDocAnswerRule(reader)` as one whole paragraph.

**Host composition (cloud build door).** Every input is a plain value the host already holds when it calls `handleHttpRequest`: the bridge and `grantedScopes` for `packageDocToolsServed`, and the listed tool names for `definitionReaderOf`. The host's `instructions` (a grant that admits authoring) take `packageDocAnswerRule(definitionReaderOf(listedToolNames))`. Its `dataOnlyInstructions` take `packageDocAnswerRule()`. That matches the open server, which names a reader only under `authoringToolsServed`. The served-check is the same predicate `registerPackageDocTools` registers from (`mcp-http-tools.ts:3345`): the bridge carries both doc members, and the grant is `data:read` or undefined. It reads the right thing for any host whose doc tools come from the bridge, which is how the platform's `runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-docs.ts` serves them.

**Byte-identical default text.** This holds by construction. In `packageDocAnswerRule` only the signature line changed, from `(definitionReader: string | undefined)` to `export … (definitionReader?: string)`, and every body line is diff context. `definitionReaderServed` keeps the `authoringToolsServed` gate and the same `Set` + `find` over the same tuple, in the same order. `openServerInstructions` and its call site are untouched. The #35442 pins (`mcp-package-doc-tools-35442.test.ts`) are not flipped.

**Public surface.** The `index.ts` diff adds exactly four value exports and no types. `mcp-http-tools.ts` is not in the diff. The three declarations newly marked `export` in `mcp-server-runtime.ts` can be reached only through the barrel, because `exports` has only `.`. The signatures:
- `packageDocAnswerRule(definitionReader?: string): string`. An omitted or empty reader gives the "not checked" form.
- `definitionReaderOf(toolNames)`, which takes an `Iterable` of `string` and returns `string | undefined`. It picks in tuple order, not input order, and the test pins that.
- `packageDocToolsServed(bridge, options?)`, which takes a `Partial` `McpDataBridge` (or `undefined`) and `RegisterObjectToolsOptions` and returns `boolean`. Both parameter types were already exported from the barrel.

No internal type leaks.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/mcp': patch` is right. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, the level follows the `Metadata-protocol` kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". The `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` self-test pins this exact pair: `yes (widening)` with `none` reads `none-clean`, which is `patch`. `none` is the correct kind, because nothing a metadata author can write changes. Check Changeset is green on this head.

Declaration lines: `Clause-②:` and `Metadata-protocol:` start a line in both the PR body and the changeset body. Main's reader reads value `yes`, arm `null` (a bare `yes` is a valid widening declaration), and kind `none`. `yes` is the right value, since the change widens a published package's export set and removes nothing. No `Skills-docs:` line is owed, because the kind is `none` and there is no `(narrowing)` arm.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report: `open_questions` and `out_of_scope_findings` are empty, and security reads `none`. Two deviations are noted: the claim line copied verbatim (that is S1 below) and the commit-trailer form.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. There is no data path; the exports are pure string and predicate helpers.
- Security: no runtime permission or grant behaviour changes. `packageDocToolsServed` is a read-only predicate that already gated registration.
- Author: the PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no separate author note is needed.
- Docs-drift row (`content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx` via `get_metadata_item`): the literal is unchanged, so there is no drift.
- CI when read: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Build Core are green. The Test Core shards, Type Check workspace/consumer and ESLint were still running. The landing check still needs them green.

### Findings

**S1 (should-fix): the declaration line miscounts the widening.** The PR body and the changeset both say `Clause-②: yes — widening: two new exported symbols on the published @objectstack/mcp barrel`, but the barrel gains four: `packageDocAnswerRule`, `packageDocToolsServed`, `definitionReaderOf` and `DEFINITION_READER_TOOL_NAMES`. The line was copied verbatim from the claim, which was written before the design added the last two. The changeset line ships into `packages/mcp/CHANGELOG.md`, and fixing an error in a released entry takes a dedicated docs-only PR later. Fix: change "two" to "four" in the changeset and the PR-body line. The value `yes` and the level stay the same. This touches only the prose face, so this record carries over a changeset-only head move (`Regen-provenance:`).

**N1 (nit): the README does not name the new exports.** `packages/mcp/README.md` § "The `initialize` instructions" describes the answer-order rule and says a host's own text is "served exactly as written". One sentence there pointing a host at `packageDocAnswerRule`, `packageDocToolsServed` and `definitionReaderOf` would make the card's purpose discoverable. This is a prose-face change that can ride with S1's commit.

**N2 (nit): host guidance for `dataOnlyInstructions`.** The jsdoc says to pass "the reader its connection lists". It could also say that the data-only text takes `packageDocAnswerRule()`, since a grant without `metadata:write` lists no reader. Otherwise a host could feed its full registry's names into `definitionReaderOf` for that text. No code change is needed.

**N3 (nit): `DEFINITION_READER_TOOL_NAMES` is now a published `as const` tuple.** Its members and their order are part of the public type, so adding a reader later is a `Clause-②: yes` widening, not an internal edit. Accepted, because the card asked for the reader-name list.

No must-fix.

The barrel now exports `packageDocAnswerRule`, `definitionReaderOf`, `DEFINITION_READER_TOOL_NAMES` (from `mcp-server-runtime.ts`) and `packageDocToolsServed` (already `export`ed at `mcp-http-tools.ts:3308`, so that file is not in the diff). `RegisterObjectToolsOptions` and `McpDataBridge`, the types a host needs to call `packageDocToolsServed`, were already on the barrel. `files: ["dist", …]` ships them.

Patch for a widening of `@objectstack/mcp` is right.

**Note (no action owed):** `definitionReaderOf(toolNames: Iterable<string>)` would accept a bare string and iterate its characters. It returns `undefined` then, which is the safe answer ("not checked"), so this needs no change.
